findings.title: POST /waterings returns 500 when litres is 1e309
findings.steps: Signed in, POST {"bed_id":1,"litres":1e309} as raw JSON
findings.evidence: curl: 'Internal Server Error 500'. The string form "1e309" is correctly rejected with 422, so the bug is only in how the JSON number is handled.

findings.title: Huge bed_id or watering id gives 500 instead of 4xx
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error on all three
findings.evidence: curl returned 'Internal Server Error 500' each time. Likely SQLite integer overflow because the new id params have no upper bound.

findings.title: Water now has no timeout and no idempotency, so a retry after a timeout records two waterings
findings.where: Beds page, Water now / Save watering
findings.steps: Click Water now while the API is slow or hanging; wait, then click again (or the first request finishes late)
findings.expected: Request fails after 10 s with a visible error, and a retry makes one watering
findings.actual: The api client has no timeout, so the button stays 'Watering…' and disabled for as long as the server hangs. Each POST inserts a new row with no idempotency key or dedupe, so a retry after a lost response records a duplicate.
findings.evidence: useApiClient/useApiFetch set no timeout (grep finds no 'timeout'). create_watering always INSERTs. Two POSTs of {bed_id:1} a second apart created two rows (ids 3 and 7).

findings.title: Waterings page and dashboard 'Recent waterings' error states have no retry
findings.steps: Make GET /api/waterings fail (server down or 5xx) and open /waterings or the dashboard
findings.expected: Error message with a Retry button that refetches without reloading
findings.actual: Only an AlertMessage is shown, with no retry control. The dashboard doesn't even destructure refresh for waterings.
findings.evidence: waterings.vue shows <AlertMessage v-if="wateringsError"> and no button. index.vue: const { data: waterings, error: wateringsError } = wateringsResult (no refresh).

findings.title: Waterings page hides a failed beds load; the bed filter silently offers only 'All beds'
findings.expected: An error saying beds couldn't load, with a retry
findings.actual: The beds error is ignored and the select shows only 'All beds', so filtering by bed is impossible and nothing explains why
findings.evidence: waterings.vue: const { data: beds } = bedsResult (error never read); options come from beds ?? []

findings.title: Record past watering form overflows at 375 px
findings.where: Beds page, Record past watering form
findings.steps: At 375 px width, open 'Record past watering' on a bed
findings.actual: The .water-form grid is 1fr 1fr auto (date, litres, and two buttons on one row) with no mobile media query. The date input's intrinsic width plus 'Save watering' and 'Cancel' don't fit in ~300 px.
findings.evidence: main.css .water-form grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr auto; no @media rule for .water-form

findings.title: Long unbroken bed names overflow the new watering tables on mobile
findings.steps: Create a bed with a 60-character name and no spaces, water it, and view /waterings at 375 px
findings.expected: Text wraps and the page has no horizontal scroll
findings.actual: The bed name cell has no overflow-wrap and the table isn't in a scroll container, so the 4-column table widens the page
findings.evidence: No overflow-wrap/word-break anywhere in main.css; .table is width:100% with no wrapper

findings.title: Invalid ?bed= query shows raw technical error; filter select contradicts the URL
findings.expected: Ignore the invalid filter or show a friendly message with a way to recover
findings.actual: Page shows 'Query.bed id: Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer'. The select shows 'All beds' while 'Clear filter' is visible.
findings.evidence: SSR HTML of /waterings?bed=abc contains that text and no list

findings.title: Bed filter doesn't follow URL changes on the same page
findings.steps: Open /waterings?bed=1, then click 'Waterings' in the nav (to /waterings)
findings.actual: bedFilter is read from route.query only once at setup, so the URL says all beds while the list stays filtered to bed 1
findings.evidence: waterings.vue: const bedFilter = ref(route.query.bed …) with no watch on route.query

findings.title: Absurd dates and tiny amounts accepted and shown badly
findings.steps: POST {"bed_id":1,"watered_on":"0001-01-01","litres":2}; POST litres 0.001; POST litres true
findings.expected: Reject implausible dates and non-numeric types, or display them faithfully
findings.actual: Year 0001 is accepted and listed as '1 Jan 1'. 0.001 L is accepted but formatLitres displays '0 L'. litres:true is stored as 1 L.
findings.evidence: 201 responses. /waterings showed '1 Jan 1 North bed 2 L'.

findings.title: 'Today' differs between browser and server time zones
findings.steps: Use a browser whose local date is ahead of the server's, and save a past watering dated today (the default)
findings.actual: The server checks date.today() in its own zone and returns 'Watering date cannot be in the future.' Also, 'Water now' stores watered_on from the server's local date but watered_at in UTC, so the date and time can disagree.
findings.evidence: schemas.WateringIn.not_in_future uses date.today(); the form defaults to the browser-local todayIso(). waterings.py mixes now.astimezone().date() with a UTC time.
